title: Winner of the Linked List Game
summary: Given a linked list with even length, where odd-indexed nodes have odd integers and even-indexed nodes have even integers, compare each pair of nodes.
statement: Given a linked list with even length, where odd-indexed nodes have odd integers and even-indexed nodes have even integers, compare each pair of nodes. The 'Odd' team scores a point if the odd-indexed node is higher, and the 'Even' team scores a point if the even-indexed node is higher. Return 'Odd' if the 'Odd' team has more points, 'Even' if the 'Even' team has more points, and 'Tie' if the scores are equal.
constraints: The nonempty linked list has even length and is read in consecutive node pairs.
The Even team scores when the even-indexed value is larger; Odd scores when the following odd-indexed value is larger.
Return Even, Odd, or Tie according to total points.
reference_solution:
def linked_list_pair_game(head):
    even=odd=0;node=head
    while node:
        if node.val>node.next.val:even+=1
        elif node.val<node.next.val:odd+=1
        node=node.next.next
    return 'Even' if even>odd else 'Odd' if odd>even else 'Tie'

    if head.val<head.next.val:return 'Odd'
    return 'Tie'
hints: Each even-indexed node is paired only with its immediate successor.
Compare their values and update one of two point totals.
Advance by two nodes after every comparison.
The traversal visits every declared pair exactly once, so comparing the final totals gives the game result.
